decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for first work zone action?
cards.back: On approaching a work zone, first slow down and look for instructions for moving through it safely.

cards.front: What is the rule for dotted continuation?
cards.back: A solid white or yellow line that becomes short dotted dashes continues the line through an intersection or interchange.

cards.front: What is the rule for remain in lane?
cards.back: Stay between lane lines except when turning, exiting the highway or changing lanes.

cards.front: What is the rule for white line meaning?
cards.back: White lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction and can mark the right pavement edge.

cards.front: What is the rule for broken white crossing?
cards.back: A broken white lane line may be crossed for a lane change after signaling and checking that it is safe.

cards.front: What is the rule for solid white crossing?
cards.back: A solid white line can mark the road edge or separate same-direction lanes, and should not be crossed except to avoid danger.

cards.front: What is the rule for double white prohibition?
cards.back: Crossing double solid white lines separating same-direction lanes is prohibited.

cards.front: What is the rule for yellow line meaning?
cards.back: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic and can mark the left edge of divided highways or one-way streets.

cards.front: What is the rule for broken yellow passing?
cards.back: Stay right of a broken yellow line except for a temporary safe pass of a vehicle ahead.

cards.front: What is the rule for mixed yellow lines?
cards.back: With paired solid and broken yellow lines, a driver beside the solid line may not cross, while a driver beside the broken line may cross for a safe pass.

cards.front: What is the rule for double yellow passing prohibition?
cards.back: Two solid yellow lines prohibit crossing to pass another vehicle.

cards.front: What is the rule for double yellow left turn?
cards.back: The general double-yellow rule described on this page allows a safe left turn across those lines.

cards.front: What is the rule for white lane arrows?
cards.back: White pavement arrows indicate lane directions or restrictions.

cards.front: What is the rule for stop and yield lines?
cards.back: A stop line is a solid white line across the approach, while a yield line is a row of adjacent triangles.

cards.front: What is the rule for crosswalk definition?
cards.back: A crosswalk uses white lines or other distinct pavement materials or markings to guide pedestrians across a traffic lane.

cards.front: What is the rule for crosswalk locations?
cards.back: Crosswalks may occur at intersections or at locations such as transit stops, schools, trails and commercial areas.

cards.front: What is the rule for stop behind crossing line?
cards.back: When a sign, signal or crossing pedestrian requires stopping, stop behind the stop, yield or crosswalk line.

cards.front: What is the rule for channelizing island?
cards.back: A channelizing island guides traffic along specified paths and keeps vehicles out of the island area.

cards.front: What is the rule for island prohibition?
cards.back: Do not drive over or park on a channelizing island unless a police officer directs you to do so.

cards.front: What is the rule for crossing guard instructions?
cards.back: Be prepared to stop for crossing guards and children, and obey the guard’s signals.

cards.front: What is the rule for crossing guard cues?
cards.back: Crosswalk warnings, reflective vests and handheld stop paddles are cues that a crossing guard or children may be in the road.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for diamond lane restriction?
cards.back: A white diamond on the pavement indicates a special lane restriction such as bus-only or high-occupancy-vehicle use.

cards.front: What is the rule for sharrow purpose?
cards.back: Shared-lane markings help bicyclists choose position and direction in a lane shared with motor vehicles.

cards.front: What is the rule for sharrow versus bicycle lane?
cards.back: A sharrow calls for watching for bicyclists and allowing passing room, and is different from a bicycle-lane marking.

cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle lane description?
cards.back: Bicycle lanes are intended for bicyclists and are typically five feet wide with solid white borders, signs and pavement markings.

cards.front: What is the rule for crossing a bicycle lane?
cards.back: Motor vehicles may drive in a bicycle lane only to turn onto or off the road and must check carefully for bicycles before crossing.

cards.front: What is the rule for advisory bicycle lane?
cards.back: Dashed advisory bicycle lanes allow motor vehicles to use that space when necessary only after yielding to bicyclists.

cards.front: What is the rule for green conflict pavement?
cards.back: Green pavement marks potential bicycle and motor-vehicle conflicts and calls for checking for bicycles before crossing.

cards.front: What is the rule for keep green pavement clear?
cards.back: Do not stop on green pavement at a red light.

cards.front: What is the rule for red transit pavement?
cards.back: Red pavement identifies transit travel lanes or station stops for public-transport systems.

cards.front: What is the rule for keep right exceptions?
cards.back: On a road with multiple lanes in your direction, drive in the right lane except to pass, turn left or avoid a blocked right lane.

cards.front: What is the rule for no intersection lane change?
cards.back: Changing lanes inside an intersection is illegal and dangerous.

cards.front: What is the rule for limited shoulder travel?
cards.back: A breakdown lane generally cannot be used for travel or passing, except where posted highway rules allow travel during specified times.

cards.front: What is the rule for blind curve?
cards.back: At a curve with an obstructed view, slow down and remain to the right.

cards.front: What is the rule for restricted lane exception?
cards.back: Do not enter a posted restricted lane except when preparing a turn.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for signal movement changes?
cards.back: Signal when stopping or changing movement so pedestrians and drivers have time to react.

cards.front: What is the rule for hand signals when needed?
cards.back: If electronic signals fail, use hand signals through the driver-side window.

cards.front: What is the rule for left hand signal?
cards.back: The depicted straight arm extending outward through the driver window signals a left turn.

cards.front: What is the rule for right hand signal?
cards.back: The depicted arm bent upward at the elbow signals a right turn.

cards.front: What is the rule for slow or stop hand signal?
cards.back: The depicted arm angled downward signals slowing or stopping.

cards.front: What is the rule for signal occasions?
cards.back: Signal lane changes, intersection or driveway turns, departures from the curb, moves to the roadside and expressway entries or exits.

cards.front: What is the rule for cancel completed signal?
cards.back: Cancel the directional signal after completing the maneuver.

cards.front: What is the rule for look signal move?
cards.back: Before turning, merging, entering traffic or changing lanes, check mirrors and the relevant blind spot, then signal and move.

cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle arm signals?
cards.back: Bicyclists may signal with either arm.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for divided highway?
cards.back: A divided highway has separate roadways for opposing traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for controlled access?
cards.back: Controlled-access expressways or freeways have no signals or intersections and use ramps at interchanges for entry and exit.

cards.front: What is the rule for plan entry and exit?
cards.back: Choose the proper lane well before entering or leaving a highway.

cards.front: What is the rule for entering driver yields?
cards.back: Yield to vehicles already traveling on the highway when entering.

cards.front: What is the rule for match highway traffic?
cards.back: Increase speed on highway entry to match existing traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for missed exit response?
cards.back: After missing an exit, continue to the next one rather than stopping or backing on the highway.

cards.front: What is the rule for advance exit signal?
cards.back: Signal a highway exit at least five hundred feet before the exit ramp.

cards.front: What is the rule for exit ramp caution?
cards.back: Watch for slow or stopped ramp traffic and slow to the posted ramp limit while leaving the highway.

cards.front: What is the rule for highway vehicle fitness?
cards.back: The vehicle must be mechanically sound and capable of highway speed before highway travel.

cards.front: What is the rule for multilane highway use?
cards.back: On an expressway with at least three lanes in one direction, the manual assigns slower travel to the right, faster travel to the middle and passing to the far left.

cards.front: What is the rule for centered highway lane?
cards.back: Drive centered within the lane and use mirrors, blind-spot checks and signals for changes.

cards.front: What is the rule for avoid blind spot travel?
cards.back: Avoid lingering in another driver’s blind spot and pass through it safely as promptly as possible.

cards.front: What is the rule for large vehicle blind spots?
cards.back: Large vehicles have blind spots at the sides, front and rear, so avoid driving immediately around them or following a truck or bus closely.

cards.front: What is the rule for highway roadside awareness?
cards.back: Watch for entering vehicles and for vehicles or people in the breakdown lane.

cards.front: What is the rule for no weaving?
cards.back: Do not weave through highway traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for highway fatigue rest?
cards.back: When prolonged highway driving causes fatigue, leave at the next exit, rest stop or service area.

cards.front: What is the rule for shoulder travel exit check?
cards.back: Before exiting where breakdown-lane travel is allowed, check to the right and inspect the right blind spot.

cards.front: What is the rule for long trip rest interval?
cards.back: On a long trip, stop and stretch every two hours or one hundred miles.

cards.front: What is the rule for highway breakdown response?
cards.back: For a highway breakdown, move as far from the travel lane onto the shoulder as possible and stay in the vehicle rather than standing near traffic or in the breakdown lane.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for intersection definition?
cards.back: An intersection is where at least two roadways meet.

cards.front: What is the rule for multiple turn lanes?
cards.back: Follow signs and markings where several turn lanes are provided.

cards.front: What is the rule for avoid blocking intersection?
cards.back: Do not enter an intersection or crosswalk unless there is enough room to pass completely through safely.

cards.front: What is the rule for intersection bicycle check?
cards.back: Before proceeding at an intersection, look twice for bicycles and allow ample space.

cards.front: What is the rule for turning yields to straight bicycle?
cards.back: A turning driver must yield to a bicyclist traveling straight through the intersection and must not cut in front.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for planned turn?
cards.back: Plan a turn ahead of time rather than turning suddenly.

cards.front: What is the rule for turn signal distances?
cards.back: Signal at least one hundred feet before a turn, or at least five hundred feet before a turn on a highway.

cards.front: What is the rule for signal before braking?
cards.back: It is best to signal a turn before braking so following drivers know the intended maneuver.

cards.front: What is the rule for turn preparation?
cards.back: Before turning, slow down, check mirrors and the turning-side blind spot and yield where required.

cards.front: What is the rule for finish turn before lane change?
cards.back: Complete the turn into the proper lane and make any needed lane change only afterward.

cards.front: What is the rule for starting turn lane?
cards.back: For a right turn start from the far-right lane, and for a left turn start from the lane nearest the center.

cards.front: What is the rule for avoid wide turn?
cards.back: Do not swing out of the lane or turn wide through an intersection; stay centered in the lanes being left and entered.

cards.front: What is the rule for follow through on turn?
cards.back: Once a turn has started through an intersection, complete it rather than stopping midway to change direction.

cards.front: What is the rule for right turn on red?
cards.back: A right turn on red requires a complete stop, yielding and no prohibiting sign.

cards.front: What is the rule for one way left on red?
cards.back: A left turn on red is allowed only between one-way streets after the same stopping and yielding required for a right turn on red.

cards.front: What is the rule for U turn permission?
cards.back: A U-turn reverses travel direction and is allowed only with a safe clear path and no No U-Turn sign.

cards.front: What is the rule for U turn lane and space?
cards.back: Start a U-turn only from the lane nearest the center line and allow enough room to avoid endangering approaching vehicles.

cards.front: What is the rule for U turn visibility?
cards.back: Do not make a U-turn near a hillcrest, curve or another place where either driver cannot see five hundred feet.

cards.front: What is the rule for shared center turn lane?
cards.back: A marked shared center lane on a two-way road is for left turns from either direction and cannot be used as a travel lane.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for three point turn conditions?
cards.back: A three-point turn is considered only on a narrow street with good visibility, light traffic, no public driveway alternative, legal permission and no other option.

cards.front: What is the rule for three point turn setup?
cards.back: Before a three-point turn, move near the right curb, signal left, check traffic and pedestrians both ways including the blind spot and wait for a twenty-to-thirty-second gap.

cards.front: What is the rule for first turning movement?
cards.back: The first three-point-turn movement is slow with a quick left steering input, stopping about two feet short of the opposite curb when perpendicular to the street.

cards.front: What is the rule for reverse turning movement?
cards.back: For the reversing portion of a three-point turn, turn the wheel fully right, check traffic and blind spots and back while looking over the right shoulder.

cards.front: What is the rule for reverse stopping point?
cards.back: Stop the reversing movement just before the opposite curb.

cards.front: What is the rule for final turning movement?
cards.back: To finish the three-point turn, recheck both directions and blind spots, signal left, select drive or first gear and accelerate to the appropriate speed.

cards.front: What is the rule for controlled backing?
cards.back: For ordinary backing, begin near the right curb, check both directions and blind spots, then reverse while looking over the right shoulder at a safe smooth speed within the lane.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, lanes, intersections, turning and initial right of way

cards.front: What is the rule for give rather than insist?
cards.back: Right of way is given rather than taken, and a driver should yield when another driver disregards the rules.

cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian already crossing?
cards.back: Yield to a pedestrian already in the roadway, including a pedestrian still in the crosswalk after your light turns green.

cards.front: What is the rule for sidewalk and driveway priority?
cards.back: A turning driver must yield to pedestrians on a sidewalk or crossing a driveway or alley.

cards.front: What is the rule for blind pedestrian priority?
cards.back: Stop completely for a blind pedestrian crossing the street and wait until the crossing is safely completed without honking or waving the person onward.

cards.front: What is the rule for uncontrolled right side priority?
cards.back: Approach an uncontrolled intersection slowly, look both ways and yield to traffic entering or approaching from the right.

cards.front: What is the rule for verify left side yielding?
cards.back: Before proceeding at an uncontrolled intersection, make sure a driver approaching from the left is actually yielding.

cards.front: What is the rule for all way order?
cards.back: At an all-way stop, yield to a vehicle that stopped first and to the vehicle on your right when both stopped together.

cards.front: What is the rule for communicate at stop?
cards.back: Eye contact at an all-way stop can help drivers understand one another’s intentions and avoid a collision.

cards.front: What is the rule for left turn yielding?
cards.back: Before any left turn, yield to approaching traffic, vehicles already in the intersection and pedestrians or bicyclists crossing the turn path.

cards.front: What is the rule for entering paved road?
cards.back: Before entering a paved through road from a private road, driveway or unpaved road, stop and yield to pedestrians, bicycles and vehicles on that road.
